frozen_problem.title: Bounded moduli charts and ghost directions for virtual resolutions
frozen_problem.statement:
Observation: The current definition of virtual resolution is so broad and it is not meaningful to parameterize, then.

Is there a well-behaved moduli theory of virtual resolutions equipped with extra structure? e.g. condition under which there exists a finite set? or space/ stacks/...?
(c.f. [Boij-Sölderberg] theory constructs a meaningful cone of Betti tables of all free complexes. Look at subcone of virtual resolutions of a given $M$)

theory.target: In the same based equal-degree binary Koszul ghost family, find the sharp single graded-degree homology test for geometric exactness, including a bounded shift/degree window, and falsify Euler-characteristic-only certification.
definitions: S=k[x,y] standard graded, B=(x,y), a>=0,d>=1, degree-d forms f,g including zeros.
F3=S(-a-2d), F2=S(-a-d)^2, F1=S(-a), F0=M=S, differentials (-g,f),(f,g),0 and identity augmentation.
H_i(n) is degree-n positive homology; r=n-a and q(r)=max(r+1,0).
e is the homogeneous gcd degree of a nonzero pair; the zero pair is separate.
Equivalence is degree-preserving chain isomorphism with fixed augmentation; based coefficients are retained, no quotient is constructed.
Virtuality means sheaf-exact positive complex on P1. Single-degree homology vanishing is not Euler vanishing.
assumptions: S=k[x,y], B=(x,y), k a field; no claim for a nonreduced coefficient base.
a>=0, d>=1; f,g homogeneous degree d, including the zero form.
F3=S(-a-2d), F2=S(-a-d)^2, F1=S(-a), F0=M=S; d3=(-g,f), d2=(f,g), d1=0 and augmentation identity.
Equivalence is degree-preserving chain isomorphism with fixed augmentation; based coefficients are retained, no quotient or classification is constructed.
Virtual means positive homology sheafifies to zero on P1; rational-point-only tests are not used.
Single-degree test means all positive homology vanish at one n, or equivalently H1 at the proposed valid cutoff, not Euler characteristic.
Finite census checks only frozen prime fields/degrees. Universal sharpness and geometric interpretation require independent proof review.
approaches_considered: Derive exact Hilbert functions from homogeneous gcd and the syzygy generator.
Reconstruct graded multiplication maps and independently enumerate homogeneous divisors.
Use Betti/Euler tail data only; retire this shortcut via cancellation certificates.
falsification_targets: The cutoff can be uniformly lowered one degree or ignore shifts.
A rational-point-only check detects every common homogeneous factor.

claims.statement: Zero positive Euler characteristic at the cutoff certifies virtuality in the frozen family. The F3 pair a=1,d=2,f=g=x^2,n=4 refutes this: H1,H2,H3 dimensions are 2,2,0 and the common zero is [0:1].
claims.falsification_condition: A wrong rank, dependent quotient/cycle vectors, nonzero d3 source or absent geometric common zero.

claims.statement: For a nonzero pair with homogeneous gcd degree e, at r=n-a>=2d-1 the homology dimensions are e,e,0. The full Hilbert formulas and separate zero-pair case are in theory.md; ordinary universal derivation pending independent review.
claims.falsification_condition: A missing syzygy, degree shift, zero-form/infinity exception or field-extension failure.

claims.statement: For every field and the fixed family, a+2d-1 is the least nonnegative single degree uniformly testing virtuality by H1 vanishing or all positive homology vanishing. Under 0<=a<=A,1<=d<=D the least uniform degree is A+2D-1.
claims.falsification_condition: A bad pair with zero H1 at the cutoff, a good pair with nonzero H1 there, or an earlier uniform degree not excluded by the stated witnesses.

claims.statement: For all pairs and r>=2d-1 the positive Euler characteristic is identically zero, being forced by the chain-space dimensions; it cannot separate any parameter points.
claims.falsification_condition: A wrong sign or dimension in the finite-chain Euler identity.

claims.statement: Independent algorithms agree on 24981 pairs and 191153 graded pieces: 17358 admissible, 7623 Euler false acceptances, 17358 one-degree-early false rejections, eight power controls and twelve bounded windows with 64 smaller-degree witnesses.
claims.falsification_condition: An omitted tuple, differing graded piece/stream hash, count or boundary outcome.

claims.statement: Eight F3 equal-power certificates have d independent quotient classes and d independent cycles with no boundaries at r=2d-1; all seven specified corruptions are rejected.
claims.falsification_condition: A failed vector equation, rank, field/degree check or accepted specified corruption.

claims.statement: Definition 1.1 of arXiv:1703.07631v2 requires the sheafified complex to resolve the associated sheaf, not Euler-characteristic vanishing. No degree-window or general moduli result is attributed to that definition.
claims.falsification_condition: A contrary primary definition or incorrect attribution.

progress.summary: Explicit F3 quotient/cycle bases certify dimensions 2,2,0 at n=4 for the nonvirtual pair f=g=x^2,a=1. Zero Euler characteristic cannot certify virtuality.
Replace the prior unspecified degree window by a+2d-1, or A+2D-1 for bounded shifts/degrees; exhibit two families excluding every smaller degree.
